subproblem.title: Completeness of integer multiplicity currents: a mass-summable series of IM currents has an IM sum (Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 3.13)
subproblem.statement: Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d (smooth d-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d; ∂X = X.boundary (∂X(ω) = X(dω)); X − Y is the contract subtraction (pointwise on test forms). For G ⊆ ℝ^P, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (covectorEuclideanNorm); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U is the contract structure IMRep U d; R represents X when X(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHᵈ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U), where ⟨ω, ξ⟩(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)); μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M is R.measure; X is integer multiplicity (IM, IsIntegerMultiplicity X) if some IMRep represents it. X vanishes off a set K if X(ω) = 0 for every ω whose tsupport is disjoint from K. X_j ⇀ Y (WeaklyConvergesOn) means X_j(ω) → Y(ω) for every ω. V ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained V U) means that closure V is compact and contained in U. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and let X_r ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (r ∈ ℕ) be IM with Σ_r M(X_r) < ∞ (sum in [0, ∞]). Then there is an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the real series Σ_r X_r(ω) converges to Y(ω) (HasSum), and M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r). This is Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 3.13 (completeness of the IM currents with respect to the mass semi-norms), applied to the partial sums of the series.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsOpen U → (∀ r, IsIntegerMultiplicity (X r)) → ∑' r, (X r).mass ≠ ∞ → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), HasSum (fun r => X r ω) (Y ω)) ∧ Y.mass ≤ ∑' r, (X r).mass
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 3.13 and its printed proof (chapter-06.txt lines 901–935), applied to the partial sums Y_q = X_0 + ⋯ + X_{q−1}, which are Cauchy for the mass M; the steps the printed proof leaves implicit (that the densities θ_qξ_q converge in L¹, that the limit multiplicity is an integer, and the identification of approximate tangent planes) are written out. Tools: the siblings (C1) the reused accepted sibling dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support: for open U, X ∈ 𝒟_d(U) and an IMRep R in U representing X, M_W(X) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, and spt X = U ∩ spt μ_R. and (IMC) the reused accepted sibling cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub: (a) if U is open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U are Borel and Hᵈ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, then for Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x iff M' has (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d · x Q); (b) if U is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and E is Borel, there are A ∈ 𝒟_d(U) and an IMRep R' in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ that represents A (so μ_{R'} = μ_R⌞E); (c) if U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_d(U) are IM, then A − B is IM; (d) for every IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in any U and Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every d-covector α. (UOD) the reused accepted sibling dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual: for all P, n there is a continuous linear map L from n-vectors to n-covectors such that for every n-vector ξ and subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α, |L(ξ)| ≤ 1 and ξ(L(ξ)) = 1. The zero current of any degree d in any U is IM: the IMRep with carrier ∅, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents it (∅ is Borel and countably d-rectifiable by Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, and every integral or a.e. condition over ∅ holds trivially). For X ∈ 𝒟_d(U), ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) and an open (or arbitrary) G ⊇ tsupport ω: |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖·M_G(X), where ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞. Indeed if ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0 (|·| is a norm: an alternating map vanishing on all increasing tuples of standard basis vectors is 0), and otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ are admissible for M_G(X). Notation: for an n-vector ζ (MultiVector P n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors) let |ζ|* := sup{ζ(α) : |α| ≤ 1}, the dual norm; ⟨ω, ζ⟩(x) := ζ(x)(ω(x)); Hⁿ := μHE[n]; Λ := Σ_r M(X_r) < ∞.
1. The current Y. By the mass inequality, Σ_r |X_r(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖Λ < ∞, so Y(ω) := Σ_r X_r(ω) is an absolutely convergent series (HasSum), linear in ω. If ω_k → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_k 0), then ω_k → 0 uniformly (the derivative of order 0), hence ‖ω_k‖ → 0 (all norms on the finite-dimensional space of covectors are equivalent), and |Y(ω_k)| ≤ ‖ω_k‖Λ → 0; so Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U). If ω is admissible for M(Y) = M_U(Y), then Y(ω) = Σ_r X_r(ω) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r), so M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r). It remains to show that Y is IM.
2. Densities of the X_r. Fix IMReps R_r = (M_r, θ_r, ξ_r) of X_r. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_r, ξ_r(x) is a unit orientation of a subspace (IMRep.orients), so by (UOD) |ξ_r(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α and ξ_r(x)(L(ξ_r(x))) = 1 with |L(ξ_r(x))| ≤ 1; hence |ξ_r(x)|* = 1. More generally |ζ|* = 1 for every unit orientation ζ of a subspace. Put η_r := θ_rξ_r on M_r and η_r := 0 off M_r. Then X_r(ω) = ∫⟨ω, η_r⟩ dHⁿ, and by (C1) ∫|η_r|* dHⁿ = ∫_{M_r} θ_r dHⁿ = μ_{R_r}(U) = M(X_r). Let E := ⋃_r M_r (Borel, countably n-rectifiable). By monotone convergence ∫ Σ_r|η_r|* dHⁿ = Λ < ∞, so η := Σ_r η_r converges absolutely Hⁿ-a.e., η = 0 off E, ∫|η|* dHⁿ ≤ Λ, and by dominated convergence (dominating function ‖ω‖Σ_r|η_r|*) Y(ω) = Σ_r∫⟨ω, η_r⟩ dHⁿ = ∫⟨ω, η⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
3. Partial sums are IM. Let Y_0 := 0 and Y_{q+1} := Y_q − (0 − X_q) (contract subtraction), so Y_q(ω) = Σ_{r<q} X_r(ω). By the remark on zero currents and (IMC)(c), every Y_q is IM; fix an IMRep R'_q = (N_q, ϑ_q, ζ_q) of Y_q and put η'_q := ϑ_qζ_q on N_q, 0 off N_q; as in step 2, |ζ_q|* = 1 Hⁿ-a.e. on N_q. Let H_q := Σ_{r<q} η_r.
4. Uniqueness of densities: H_q = η'_q Hⁿ-a.e. Let A_q := M_0 ∪ ⋯ ∪ M_{q−1} ∪ N_q and ν_q := Hⁿ⌞A_q, a measure finite on compact subsets of U (Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for each IMRep, as θ ≥ 1). Z := H_q − η'_q vanishes off A_q, is locally ν_q-integrable on U, and ∫⟨ω, Z⟩ dν_q = Y_q(ω) − Y_q(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). For a fixed covector α and a smooth g with compact support in U, ω := gα ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) gives ∫ g·Z(α) dν_q = 0; by the fundamental lemma on the open set U (IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero), Z(α) = 0 ν_q-a.e. on U. Applying this to the finitely many covectors of a basis gives Z = 0 ν_q-a.e., i.e. H_q = η'_q Hⁿ-a.e. (both vanish off A_q ⊆ U). In particular |H_q(x)|* = ϑ_q(x)·1_{N_q}(x) ∈ ℕ for Hⁿ-a.e. x.
5. Integer multiplicity. Let Z₀ be a Borel Hⁿ-null set containing the countably many exceptional sets of steps 2–4 (all r and q). For x ∉ Z₀: H_q(x) → η(x) and |H_q(x)|* ∈ ℕ for all q, and a convergent sequence of integers is eventually constant, so θ(x) := |η(x)|* ∈ ℕ and |H_q(x)|* = θ(x) for all q ≥ q₀(x). Put θ := 0 on Z₀, M₊ := {x ∈ E ∖ Z₀ : θ(x) ≥ 1} (Borel, using Borel representatives of η), ξ := η/θ on M₊ and ξ := 0 elsewhere.
6. Orientation. For x ∈ M₊ and q ≥ q₀(x): ϑ_q(x)1_{N_q}(x) = θ(x) ≥ 1, so x ∈ N_q, ϑ_q(x) = θ(x) and ζ_q(x) = η'_q(x)/θ(x) = H_q(x)/θ(x) → η(x)/θ(x) = ξ(x). By (IMC)(a) applied to M₊ ∩ N_q ⊆ M₊ and to M₊ ∩ N_q ⊆ N_q (both ambient sets have locally finite Hⁿ-measure in U: Hⁿ(M₊) ≤ ∫|η|* dHⁿ ≤ Λ, and Hⁿ(N_q ∩ K) < ∞), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M₊ ∩ N_q and every subspace Q, M₊ has approximate tangent space Q at x iff N_q has. Let Z₁ be the union over q of these Hⁿ-null exceptional sets and of the null sets where the orientation property of R'_q fails (M₊ is not changed). For x ∈ M₊ ∖ Z₁ and q ≥ q₀(x), N_q has an approximate tangent space Q_x at x of which ζ_q(x) is a unit orientation (IMRep.orients for R'_q), so M₊ has the approximate tangent space Q_x at x (it is unique, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, so Q_x does not depend on q), and all ζ_q(x), q ≥ q₀(x), lie in the two-point set {e_x, −e_x}, e_x := τ₁∧⋯∧τ_n for one fixed orthonormal basis τ of Q_x (two orthonormal bases of Q_x differ by an orthogonal matrix of determinant ±1). This set is closed, so ξ(x) = lim_q ζ_q(x) ∈ {±e_x}: ξ(x) is a unit orientation of the approximate tangent space of M₊ at x.
7. The IMRep of Y. (M₊, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U: M₊ ⊆ E ⊆ U is Borel and countably n-rectifiable (subset of E); θ is measurable and θ ≥ 1 on M₊; ∫_{M₊∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫|η|* dHⁿ ≤ Λ < ∞; ξ is Hⁿ⌞M₊-a.e. strongly measurable (a quotient of measurable functions), and by step 6 it orients at every x ∈ M₊ ∖ Z₁, i.e. Hⁿ-a.e. on M₊ (the orients field is an a.e. statement). It represents Y: η = θξ on M₊, and η = 0 Hⁿ-a.e. off M₊ (θ = |η|* = 0 on E ∖ (M₊ ∪ Z₀), η = 0 off E), so ∫_{M₊} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫⟨ω, η⟩ dHⁿ = Y(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Hence Y is IM. ∎
proof_key_steps: |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖M(X) makes Y(ω) := Σ_r X_r(ω) an absolutely convergent series defining a current with M(Y) ≤ Σ M(X_r).
The densities η_r = θ_rξ_r have ∫|η_r|* = M(X_r) by (C1) and |ξ_r|* = 1, so η = Σ η_r converges in L¹ and a.e. and represents Y.
Partial sums Y_q are IM ((IMC)(c)); the fundamental lemma identifies their IMRep densities with Σ_{r<q}η_r a.e., so |Σ_{r<q}η_r| is integer-valued.
The a.e. limit θ = |η|* of integer-valued functions is an integer; on M₊ = {θ ≥ 1} the unit orientations ζ_q converge to ξ = η/θ.
Tangent locality ((IMC)(a)) identifies the approximate tangent planes of N_q and M₊, so ξ orients M₊; (M₊, θ, ξ) is an IMRep of Y.

audit.reason: Mass summability defines a sequentially continuous current with the asserted HasSum and mass bound. The fundamental lemma identifies partial-sum densities; their integer norms stabilize pointwise, and tangent locality identifies the limiting orientation. The supplied measurable carrier, multiplicity and orientation satisfy the IMRep requirements. No weak-compactness or flat-convergence conclusion is assumed.
